description: Plan v7 section 8.3 'multi-axis language-form dispatch': two axes selected independently inside ONE definition, from two different caller values. Actor.Bio is single-axis gender with two placeholders reading one value; 'Bio for {{actorGender}}' repeats the gender selector under a key that EMBEDS the selector name, so the RETURNED_KEY translation a resolution failure produces is interpolated from the caller context and therefore differs per failure mode (DefaultStrings.interpolateFailureKey, DefaultStrings.java:1391) instead of collapsing to one indistinguishable token. Books.Read pairs gender with cardinality and is loaded in Polish as well, so the cardinality half runs under a four-form plural rule set while the gender half stays constant. Race.Result pairs the two NUMERIC axes (ordinality and cardinality) in one definition, which is where a port that shares one classification step between axes diverges. Award.Announcement's alternatives select on gender while its inherited placeholders select on cardinality. Tiebreakers are null: 'en' and 'pl' share no primary language code, so no tiebreaker list is required or permitted.

Actor.Bio.commentary: Two independent gender placeholders read the same caller value.

Bio for {{actorGender}}.commentary: The key deliberately references the selector value. On a resolution failure DefaultStrings returns the key INTERPOLATED with the caller context, so each failure mode renders a different translation: a tagged Gender renders its enum name, a raw string renders itself, and an absent or null value leaves '{{actorGender}}' literal. Without that, every failure in this family would observe the same RETURNED_KEY / RESOLUTION_FAILURE token.

Race.Result.commentary: The two numeric axes in one definition. Ordinality and cardinality are the only axes that accept a bare number, so they are the pair a port is most likely to route through one shared classification step.

Award.Announcement.commentary: Alternatives select on gender; placeholders select on cardinality. The 'winner' map deliberately omits GENDER_NEUTER, which is unreachable because the NEUTER branch's translation does not reference {{winner}} -- only placeholders REFERENCED by the selected translation are resolved.
